name: UGANDA

flag.title: Flag of Uganda
flag.note: Black, yellow & red; crested crane disc

lead: Uganda sits on the equator. Winston Churchill, a British leader, called it the Pearl of Africa. Half of the world's mountain gorillas live here. So does the shoebill, a bird that looks like a pelican crossed with a dinosaur.

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: A bit bigger than the UK

geo: Uganda has no coast, yet water is everywhere. Lake Victoria, the world's second-largest freshwater lake, touches its south. The Nile starts at Jinja and flows 6,650 km north to the sea.
The Rwenzori are the Mountains of the Moon. Their peaks stay icy even on the equator.
animals: Uganda has over 1,090 bird species, nearly half of all African birds. The shoebill has a bill like a wooden clog.
Bwindi Impenetrable National Park shelters about 459 mountain gorillas. In Queen Elizabeth Park, lions climb trees and lounge in the branches.
culture: Matoke is steamed green banana. The Rolex is a chapati (flatbread) rolled around fried eggs and veggies. Its name is short for rolled eggs.
Buganda royal drummers can send messages across hills using only rhythm. The Nyege Nyege festival fills the Nile bank at Jinja with four nights of music.
history: The Buganda Kingdom began in the 14th century near Lake Victoria. It grew into one of East Africa's strongest states. Its king, the kabaka, had a big army and a fleet of canoes.
Britain made Uganda a protectorate (a land it controlled) in 1894. Uganda became free on 9 October 1962. The cruel years of ruler Idi Amin came in the 1970s.
wows: The Nile, the world's longest river, starts in Uganda.
At Murchison Falls, the whole Nile squeezes through a 7-metre gap, then drops 43 m.
Visitors can trek to see 19 gorilla families, more than in any other country.
The shoebill stands still for 30 minutes, then strikes faster than the eye can follow.
Lions in the Ishasha area climb trees from cubhood, a habit almost unique in Africa.
Bwindi, one park, holds roughly half the world's mountain gorillas.
In 2016, the government named the Rolex (egg-and-chapati snack) a tourist attraction.

myths.myth: Gorillas are fierce and attack people
myths.fact: Mountain gorillas are shy and gentle. They mostly eat leaves. Males beat their chests to show off, not to fight.

myths.myth: Hippos are too slow to catch you
myths.fact: A hippo can run about 30 km/h over short distances. That is faster than most people.
